llm.summary: This skill openly creates an autonomous agent loop, but it has broad, persistent authority and limited built-in controls, so users should review it before installing.

dimensions.detail: The plugin writes logs, watches stop files, reads OpenClaw gateway configuration, uses the gateway token, and reads device identity private-key material to request operator read/write scopes. This is local and related to sending messages, but sensitive credential use and broad operator scope are under-disclosed in the user-facing docs.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is a manual local copy into the OpenClaw extensions directory with no remote payload retrieval or package install. Once installed, it is loaded by the gateway as a persistent extension.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The docs disclose the loop, delay, stop file, logs, and DONE/HEARTBEAT_OK stop tokens, but they do not provide hard iteration limits, runtime caps, per-session approval gates, or a true agent allowlist; the fallback message can run for any agent.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The plugin registers gateway_start and agent_end hooks, maintains timers and file watchers, and can repeatedly re-trigger sessions until a stop token or stop file is present. It does not install a system service, but the autonomous loop itself is unbounded.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose matches the implementation: it sends follow-up messages after agent replies through the local OpenClaw gateway. The concern is that this can keep agents executing workspace tasks indefinitely and appears to apply broadly unless manually stopped.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only in workspaces where you intentionally want unattended agent activity. Configure narrow per-agent messages, create stop files before working on sensitive sessions, monitor the logs, and avoid using it with agents that can deploy, delete data, access secrets, or make irreversible changes without human review.
llm.findings:
[TM1] expected: The cited rm command only removes this plugin's stop file to resume the loop; it is documented stop/resume behavior, not evidence of destructive file deletion.
[P3] unexpected: The scanner's exfiltration concern is not supported by the artifact: the implementation sends configured messages to ws://127.0.0.1 on the local OpenClaw gateway, not to an external service.
[LP3] unexpected: The least-privilege concern is partly supported: the plugin needs gateway access for its purpose, but the artifacts do not clearly declare or constrain filesystem, token, device-identity, or operator read/write authority.
[EA2] expected: Autonomous re-triggering is the core advertised feature, but it remains a review concern because it can continue making agent-driven workspace changes without fresh user initiation.
[SQP-2] expected: The loop behavior is disclosed, but the active safety model relies mostly on stop files and stop tokens rather than prominent consent prompts, maximum iterations, or runtime limits.
[SQP-1] expected: The manifest accurately says it sends a follow-up after each agent reply, but it does not define trigger boundaries, termination caps, or approval checkpoints.
[SQP-3] expected: The hard-coded en-US locale is present but is a minor product-quality issue, not a material security concern.
